title: pg_dump --data-only spends hours collecting unused index definitions from a corrupted database
body: I am using PostgreSQL 18 on Debian 12. With corrupted system indexes and ignore_system_indexes=on, pg_dump --data-only still collects index definitions even though the dump does not use them. In a synthetic database with 15,000 tables and five indexes per table, the dump took 62m44.582s; about 3,474,423.683 ms was spent in the getIndexes query containing pg_get_indexdef(), pg_get_constraintdef(), and repeated pg_attribute subqueries. I have a simple patch that skips getIndexes() and flagInhIndexes() for a data-only dump, and it passes the tests.

symptoms_visible: With ignore_system_indexes=on, pg_dump --data-only takes 62m44.582s on my synthetic schema, with roughly 3,474 seconds spent in the query that reads index definitions.
N0.label: N0 prolonged data-only dump reported

symptoms_visible: While rescuing a large corrupted database, the index-definition query was still running after more than three hours.
N1.label: N1 real recovery incident confirmed

symptoms_visible: After system reindex and VACUUM FULL, the stock data-only dump still remains stuck on the index-definition work for hours.
N2_x.label: N2_x catalog maintenance aftermath

symptoms_visible: The normal data-only dump still cannot get past the lengthy index-definition query; for this recovery I only need the table data, not the schema or indexes.
N2.label: N2 data-only recovery scope established

symptoms_visible: The modified data-only pg_dump completed, and I recovered the required table data without waiting for the index-definition query.
N_terminal.label: terminal data recovered

question_patterns: Is this only a synthetic example, or did you encounter it while recovering a real database?
Have you experienced this delay in the field?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The problem is real. We encountered it while trying to rescue data from a large corrupted database.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is only a synthetic benchmark; I have not encountered catalog corruption or a blocked recovery.
It happened during recovery of a somewhat smaller corrupted production database.

question_patterns: How long did the index-definition query block the real recovery?
Did the real dump eventually get past this query?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We could not wait for the index-definition query for more than three hours.

edges.comment: Nathan asked whether the scenario was hypothetical. Andrew confirmed that it occurred during an actual rescue of a large corrupted database and that the team abandoned the index-definition query after more than three hours.

solution.intent: Repair the damaged system catalogs first by running VACUUM FULL on some or all system catalogs, then retry the ordinary data-only dump.
solution.concrete_example: Start the recovery by running VACUUM FULL on the affected system catalogs, then rerun pg_dump --data-only.

edges.comment: Álvaro suggested VACUUM FULL as a recovery starting point. Andrew reported that system reindex and VACUUM FULL had already been tried and the prolonged dump behavior remained.

question_patterns: After reindexing and VACUUM FULL, what happens when you retry the stock data-only dump?
Does catalog maintenance let the ordinary pg_dump get past the index-definition query?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. System reindex and VACUUM FULL did not change the situation; the ordinary dump still spends hours on that query.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After VACUUM FULL, the stock data-only dump completes normally in a few minutes.

edges.comment: In the same reply, Andrew volunteered that the recovery did not require schema or index definitions. That scope makes the already-proposed modified data-only dump suitable for this incident.

solution.intent: For this emergency table-data-only recovery, use the tested modified pg_dump that bypasses getIndexes() and inherited-index flagging when data-only mode is selected, then verify that the dump completes and the required data can be restored.
solution.concrete_example: Build pg_dump with the data-only guard around getIndexes() and flagInhIndexes(), run it against the corrupted database, and confirm that the output completes and restores the required table data. Keep this scoped to the recovery where schema and indexes are intentionally not being dumped.
solution.inference_hint: The thread's query analysis attributes the extreme runtime to definition-producing functions operating with a cold catalog cache and to repeated pg_attribute scans when system indexes are ignored. The reporter supplied the query and timings but did not formulate that detailed mechanism. The verified incident resolution was the narrower modified data-only pg_dump; whether PostgreSQL should generally omit getIndexes() remained subject to dependency-ordering concerns.

edges.comment: Andrew reported that a modified pg_dump recovered the data. The final move is intentionally scoped to this emergency data-only rescue rather than treating omission of index discovery as an established general upstream design.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the incident cause: pg_dump --data-only still performs getIndexes() catalog work, and with corrupted or ignored system indexes its index/constraint definition calls and repeated catalog access can take hours even though this recovery does not need schema or index definitions.
The recommendation must be grounded in the measured query runtime, the real three-hour recovery stall, and the fact that only table data was required.

For this resolved incident, must recommend the tested modified data-only pg_dump that bypasses index collection, while keeping the recommendation scoped to emergency data recovery rather than asserting that indexes can always be ignored without dependency analysis.
Must not present system reindex or VACUUM FULL as the fix; both were tried in this case and the stock dump remained stalled.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the modified dump completes and that the required data can be recovered before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical PostgreSQL user capable of reproducing catalog-query performance problems, building patched pg_dump binaries, and supplying source-level patches and server timing logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and evidence-driven; provides reproducible SQL, exact timings, and patches, then answers operational questions directly.
